headline: Microsoft refreshes Surface Pro & Laptop with Snapdragon X2 Plus chips
summary: The new Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch boast up to 18% more efficient battery performance and over 60% faster graphics, but come with a higher starting price.
details: Microsoft has updated its smaller Surface Pro and Surface Laptop models with Qualcomm's latest Snapdragon X2 Plus chips. These refreshed devices promise significant performance gains, including up to 18% better battery efficiency and over 60% faster graphics.

The Surface Pro 12-inch Second Edition now starts at $1,149.99, a notable increase from its previous $799.99 starting price. Similarly, the Surface Laptop 13-inch Second Edition sees its starting price jump to $1,199.99 from $899.99.

A key factor in the price increase is the removal of the 8GB RAM base model. Both new devices come standard with a minimum of 16GB of RAM, expandable up to 24GB, addressing the 'RAMageddon' concerns of previous generations.

Beyond raw performance, Microsoft claims the new chips enable up to 95% faster local AI inferencing. This translates to tangible real-world benefits like an extra hour of web browsing on the Surface Pro (up to 13 hours total) and two extra hours on the Surface Laptop (up to 18 hours total).

Display specifications see minor upgrades: the Surface Pro retains its 12-inch, 2196 x 1464 LCD at 90Hz, while the Surface Laptop features a 13-inch, 1920 x 1280 display at 60Hz. Both now offer 500 nits of brightness, up from 400 nits.

Connectivity and ports remain largely the same, with both devices featuring two USB-C 3.2 ports. The Surface Laptop also includes a USB-A 3.2 port and a 3.5mm headphone jack. Both support Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4.

Microsoft is also reintroducing the black color option for both devices, alongside platinum silver and violet. The Surface Pro 12-inch will be available with an optional 5G configuration, and both will be offered to commercial customers.

headline_marked: Apple Podcasts [[adds video support]] for paid subscribers
headline: Apple Podcasts adds video support for paid subscribers
summary: Creators can now offer exclusive video content to their subscribers, enhancing the podcast experience beyond audio.
details: Apple has announced a significant update for its Podcasts platform, enabling creators to offer video content as part of their subscription offerings.
This new feature allows podcasters to provide an enriched experience for their paying audience, moving beyond traditional audio formats.
The integration of video is expected to open up new avenues for content monetization and audience engagement within the Apple Podcasts ecosystem.
This move positions Apple Podcasts to compete more directly with other platforms that already offer video content alongside audio.
caption:
Apple Podcasts is leveling up its subscription game by adding video support for creators.

Apple has announced a significant update for its Podcasts platform, enabling creators to offer video content as part of their subscription offerings.

This new feature allows podcasters to provide an enriched experience for their paying audience, moving beyond traditional audio formats.

The integration of video is expected to open up new avenues for content monetization and audience engagement within the Apple Podcasts ecosystem.

This move positions Apple Podcasts to compete more directly with other platforms that already offer video content alongside audio.
